body.p: Claims 1-2, 5-12, 14-21, and 23-25 are pending in the application. Claim 13 is canceled herein, and claims 23-25 are newly added.
The applicants thank the Examiner for entering the after-final amendment, and for determining that the amendment overcame the claim objections and the rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b).
The Examiner rejects claims 1-2, 5-10, 12-15, 17-21, and 23 under 35
U.S.C. 103 over Asada et al. (USPA 2007/0055163, hereinafter Asada) and Banet et al. (USPA 2017/0188973, hereinafter Banet).
The applicants respectfully traverse this rejection in view of amended independent claims 1, 9, and 18.
Each of the independent claims is amended to specifically recite that the
determination of the blood pressure value based on the AC component of the PPG signal occurs when the applied force reaches a predetermined force value.

This amendment finds support at page 2, lines 29-31, and page 3, lines 21-25. The specification refers to determining the blood pressure value at a "specific" force, and provides an example (predetermined) minimum force level of 15N, and an example optimal force level of 17.25N (page 7, lines 1-4).

The combination of Asada and Banet does not disclose monitoring the measured force and, when the measured force reaches a predetermined force level, mapping the extracted information from the AC component to a blood pressure value.
The conventional technique for estimating blood pressure comprises
monitoring the PPG signal, then determining the MAP as the pressure being applied when the AC component of the PPG signal is at a maximum.

The applicants teach and claim an opposite technique. Instead of monitoring the AC component of the PPG signal to identify when a maximum value occurs, the applicants monitor the force being applied until it reaches a given force level.

Instead of determining the blood pressure based on the force that is applied when the AC component of the PPG signal is maximal, the applicants determine the blood pressure based on the AC component of the PPG signal at a given force value.
The Examiner acknowledges that Asada does not determine blood pressure
based on the AC component of the PPG signal.
"Asada does not explicitly teach the invention wherein information is
extracted regarding a blood volume pulse from an AC component of an output
signal of the PPG sensor.
"Banet teaches the invention wherein information is extracted regarding a
blood volume pulse from an AC component of an output signal of the PPG sensor (Paragraph 0106: application of pressure to identify AC components).
Banet teaches analogous art in the technology of PPG waveform analysis
(Abstract).
"It would have been obvious to one having skill in the art before the effective

filing date to have modified Asada in view of Banet to include extracting information from an AC component of the output of the PPG sensor, the motivation being that it is well-known that the maximum amplitude of the pulsations corresponds to an applied pressure equal to mean arterial
pressure (MAP)." (Office action, page 5, lines 13-22, emphasis added.)
At the text cited by the Examiner, Banet discloses:
"The Handheld Sensor 100 can also measure blood pressure according to

an alternative direct-pressure-based technique. This technique involves monitoring PPG waveforms generated by the SpO2 measuring system (i.e., by either red or infrared wavelengths emitted by the dual-emitting LED 132 and detected by the photodetector 134) while the inflatable bladders 140A,B apply pressure to the user's radial artery. Here, the applied pressure slowly reduces blood flow through the artery, causing heartbeat-induced PPG- waveform pulsations (i.e. pulsations in the RED(AC) or IR(AC) components of the PPG waveforms) to slowly increase, and then gradually decrease. As with oscillometry, the maximum amplitude of the pulsations typically corresponds to an applied pressure equal to MAP. The pulsations are completely eliminated when the applied pressure is equal to SYS, since at this pressure the radial artery is fully occluded, thus ceasing all blood flow. DIA can be determined from MAP and SYS using equations described in the above- referenced patent applications, the contents of which have been previously
incorporated herein by reference. (Banet [0106], emphasis added.)

Banet discloses the conventional technique for estimating blood pressure, wherein the amplitude of the pulsations are monitored, and when a maximum is reached, the force/pressure that caused this maximum is used to estimate the blood pressure.

In the conventional technique (Banet), it is impossible to predefine a force level at which the blood pressure is to be estimated, because the amplitude of the pulsations controls when the blood pressure is to be estimated.

Because the combination of Asada and Banet does not disclose the newly added limitation of monitoring the measured force, and, when the measured force reaches a predetermined force value, map the extracted information from the AC component of the PPG signal to a blood pressure value at the measured force.

In view of the foregoing, the applicants respectfully request that the Examiner withdraw the objection(s) and/or rejection(s) of record, allow all the pending claims, and find the application to be in condition for allowance.
